title: Refactor buffering & exporters to reduce observability flush latency and metric cardinality
creator: Aisha Kwan
description:
Summary:
We see elevated observability flush latencies and rapidly growing metric series from un-normalized labels. This ticket refactors the in-process buffering and OTLP export path to a lower-allocation, adaptive-batch design and introduces label normalization for high-cardinality metric/trace attributes. Goals: 1) reduce export flush p99 from ~120ms to <25ms under typical load, 2) reduce reported metric series by >50% for common workloads, 3) cut CPU/memory overhead from span batching/exporting.

Background & root cause analysis:
- Current exporter uses synchronous marshal + goroutine-per-export pattern with repeated map copies per span. That leads to spiky allocations and stalls under bursty traffic.
- Metric labels are emitted verbatim from callers (route, request_id, model_id), producing many unique series (observed 42M series/day on sandbox for a single service).
- OTLP exporter gRPC stream was configured with small batch sizes and immediate flush, which increased RPC overhead and latency variance.

Proposed changes (implementation outline):
1) Buffering refactor: introduce a pooled, pre-allocated ring buffer for spans/metrics with a single producer/consumer design to avoid per-span allocations. Implement zero-copy protobuf encoding path using a reusable proto marshaller.
2) Adaptive batching: use a sliding-window sampler that grows/shrinks batch sizes based on observed throughput and producer queue length to control flush latency vs throughput. Add a fast-path for single-span low-latency exports when queue is nearly empty.
3) Exporter switch to HTTP/Protobuf for hostnames where gRPC impact is high; keep gRPC as default with negotiated compression. Add configurable exporter dial priorities for Dedicated vs Hosted traffic.
4) Label normalization ruleset: whitelist labels to keep and canonicalize high-cardinality keys (strip UUIDs/hash model ids, bucket numerical IDs). Provide per-team overrides via config in the Console.
5) Metrics series sampler: when series growth exceeds threshold, automatically move low-signal series to an aggregated series and emit a cardinality-report metric.

Benchmarks (dev/staging):
- Microbench (simulated burst of 10k req/s): p99 export flush reduced from 120ms -> 18ms.
- Allocations/spans: median allocs/span down 67%, RSS for exporter worker down 15%.
- Metric cardinality: sample workload reduced unique series by 72% after normalization rules.

Trade-offs & risks:
- Normalization can hide signals if rules are too aggressive; mitigation: conservative default rules + per-service opt-out and a dry-run mode that reports what would change without dropping labels.
- HTTP/Protobuf may behave differently under certain network middleboxes; rollout via canary and fallback to gRPC if exporter errors increase.
- Pooling reduces GC pressure but requires careful object lifecycle; introduce runtime assertions and a leak detector during the rollout.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1 (this ticket): Buffer ring + pooled marshaller; unit tests and microbench harness (ENG-49822-1).
- Week 2: Adaptive batch controller + exporter HTTP path + integration tests (ENG-49822-2).
- Week 3: Label normalization library + Console config UI prototyping (ENG-49822-3).
- Week 4: Canary rollout to non-prod clusters, monitor spans_export_failures, exporter_queue_length, metric_series_count, and latency SLOs. If stable, progressive rollout to production Dedicated pool.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy canary to staging-only and one low-traffic production shard (10% traffic) with dry-run normalization.
2) Monitor: span_export_latency_p99, exporter_rpc_errors, exporter_queue_length, metric_series_count, cost-per-token for inference routes.
3) If no regressions in 48h, enable normalization in dry-run -> soft-drop -> hard-drop steps across 72h.

Observability & alerts:
- New dashboards: exporter_pipelining_overview, normalization_impact_report.
- Alerts: exporter_rpc_errors > 1% sustained for 10m; exporter_queue_length > 75th percentile threshold; sudden drop in span counts (possible data loss).

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.internal.redwood/obs/buffering-refactor-2026
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8129 (ring buffer + pooling), https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8147 (adaptive batching + exporter changes), https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2062 (normalization UI)
- Perf harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-perf-harness

Follow-ups:
- Post-rollout: add eBPF sampling for high-cost paths and correlate with exporter queue pressure (separate ticket).
- Add audit logging for normalization rules changes (security/compliance).

Acceptance criteria:
- p99 export flush latency reduced to <25ms on the staging perf harness under baseline load.
- Metric series count reduced by >=50% for evaluated workloads with default normalization rules.
- No increase in exporter RPC error rate >0.5% during the production canary.
